source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references for identity, date, edition, and claim scope. The official ISO record confirms ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 is the published second edition and distinguishes an architecture from an architecture description. Publisher and DOI records confirmed the Perry-Wolf foundation, de Silva-Balasubramaniam survey and its minimise/prevent/repair classification, Murphy-Notkin-Sullivan reflexion-model paper, Parnas software-aging paper, Eick et al. code-decay study, Rosik et al. case study, the Clements et al. second edition, the Bass-Clements-Kazman fourth edition, and the Martin title. Historical terminology is attributed rather than presented as a universal current definition. Mutable records were checked on 2026-09-06.

evidence: Reviewed high-level and lower-level element sets, partial multi-valued mapping, permitted, required, extracted, observed, convergence, divergence, absence, ambiguity, waiver, time, and version notation before use.
Checked subset, intersection, set difference, disjointness, union, empty-set, cardinality, and conformance expressions for defined operands and GitHub-renderable delimiters.
Confirmed the chapter does not use one symbol for both the worked observed set and the general observed-set definition within the same local derivation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The sets are explicitly labeled analytical models and do not stand in for the complete architecture.

evidence: Executed the finite reflexion example and independently confirmed three convergences, one divergence, no required absences, and a false conformance result.
Independently recomputed Exercise 2: convergences {(A,B),(D,C)}, divergence {(A,C)}, and required absence {(B,C)}.

Checked Example 6's stated 70 percent as an illustrative observation rather than a derived corpus statistic, and checked Example 9's counts are used only to demonstrate measurement-version confounding.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All quantities are toy or hypothetical. No example count, density, or percentage is presented as calibrated architectural risk.

evidence: Verified O equals the disjoint union of O intersect P and O minus P by exhaustive membership cases.
Verified D empty is equivalent to O being a subset of P, while A empty is equivalent to R being a subset of O.
Verified an unobserved relation in P but outside R is not included in A, preserving the distinction between permission and requirement.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The derivation is bounded to declared finite relation sets and makes no claim that extraction or intent is complete.

evidence: Reviewed empty divergence and absence sets, optional permitted relations, unmapped and multi-mapped elements, generated code, dynamic loading, sampled runtime paths, disabled features, renames, autoscaling, and changing extractors.

Reviewed emergency support access, broad identities, cross-domain data reads, schema deletion, retries, overload, partitions, recovery, shared control planes, supplier behavior, manual fallback, and retiring systems.
Reviewed adversarial metric gaming, waiver renewal, indirect dependency displacement, false precision from forced mappings, obsolete intent, rebuild recurrence, and organizational blame.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Safety, railway, privacy, security, legal, accessibility, and regulatory judgments remain assigned to authorized domain processes and people.

evidence: Traced the scope-version-mapping-observation invariant through classification, trend analysis, examples, repair, and closure.
Confirmed waived relations remain visible as divergences and authorization does not silently rewrite observation or conformance.
Confirmed every response path retains concern, rationale, owner, evidence, expiry or closure, and re-observation appropriate to the mechanism.
invariant_checking.notes: Detection, architectural consequence, and accountable disposition remain separate stages throughout.

evidence: Reviewed the set-partition argument for complete cases and confirmed convergence and divergence are disjoint.
Reviewed the count-severity counterexample: one authority-bypassing ledger write can have greater integrity consequence than one hundred benign logging imports, so counts do not generally order risk.
Reviewed the conformance limitation and confirmed it proves only a predicate over declared sets, not quality, mapping validity, observation completeness, or desirable intent.
proof_review.notes: The chapter labels theorem-like set claims, counterexamples, evidence, inference, and judgment according to their actual scope.

evidence: Audited uses of prove, truth, valid, complete, conformance, consequence, cause, severity, safety, and guarantee for scope limitations.
Confirmed correlations and trends are investigation prompts and causal claims require mechanisms plus discriminating evidence.
Confirmed the rail transfer answer expressly disclaims railway safety certification by architecture review.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No metric, detector, trace, document, waiver, or internal review is mislabeled as proof of a real system's safety or quality.

evidence: Executed snippet classify-reflexion-relations with the repository verifier under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.
Observed exit status 0, exact ordered convergence, divergence, absence, and conformance output, and empty stderr.
The chapter states that execution verifies one finite classification only and does not validate real mappings, intent, observations, or architecture.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The remaining cases are explicitly hypothetical worked reasoning, not measurements of an external system or organization.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed terminology, prescription versus observation, reflexion modeling, mapping uncertainty, multi-layer recovery, structural and behavioral erosion, data and authority, operations, organizational factors, trend interpretation, causal limits, prioritization, response choice, waivers, rule maintenance, recovery, prevention, verification, and history for conceptual coherence and bounded ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical inputs and failure paths across source, contracts, schemas, infrastructure, admission state, runtime traces, identities, deployments, incident response, suppliers, and team workflows. The chapter provides explicit actions for model versioning, mapping review, detector testing, exception expiry, risk-based prioritization, multi-layer repair evidence, and obsolete-intent correction. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth judgment; precise separation of drift, erosion, violation, conformance, aging, and debt; a derived set model; eighteen distinct misconceptions; one reproducible classifier; ten varied worked examples with explicit conclusions; and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar safety-critical rail transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks, structural validation, mathematical review, and one local Python execution do not validate an external architecture, prove observation completeness or causal attribution, certify a detector or product, establish universal severity, or provide railway, safety, clinical, legal, privacy, accessibility, cybersecurity, financial, procurement, labor, or regulatory approval.
